title: In vivo CRISPR delivery and off-target control
bottleneck: CRISPR therapies work ex vivo with edited cells reinfused, but delivering editors to the right cells inside the body, including brain, muscle, and lung, remains unsolved; lipid nanoparticles target mainly liver, and viral delivery faces AAV's immune and cargo limits. Off-target edits and long-term genotoxicity are incompletely characterized.
why_it_blocks: Most genetic diseases affect tissues beyond the liver and blood; without targeted in vivo delivery, CRISPR's curative potential stays narrow.
current_state: Tissue-targeted lipid nanoparticles, virus-like particles, and high-fidelity editors are advancing rapidly, while capsid engineering seeks to evade pre-existing immunity. Durable, specific in vivo editing of non-liver tissues is not yet clinical reality. High-fidelity editors with reduced off-target activity are advancing, but regulators will demand long-term follow-up data that does not yet exist. Delivery, not editing chemistry, is now the field's binding constraint.
